matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal); sticks cannot be rotated.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick from one character to another.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick and placing it as a vertical stick, resulting in an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For every transformation, ensure the total number of sticks stays constant.
matchstick.example: Turning ‘=’ into ‘-’ and not putting the removed horizontal stick back on the board.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after the stick relocation, before checking arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Leaving a single diagonal after taking one away from an X, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate transformed equation, before finalising the answer.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘=’ to ‘-’ and assuming the equation is solved without checking that the numbers no longer match.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonal sticks forming a valid X or V shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal stick is taken from or added to an X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from an X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’, using uppercase and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.example: Ending the response with extra text or a missing ‘Correct version of the equation:’ prefix.

matchstick.title: Diagonal stick reposition for V↔X
matchstick.principle: When a V or X appears, you can change it to the other by moving one of its diagonal sticks to a new position (preserving orientation) so that the resulting shape is a valid X or V.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the numeric imbalance can be fixed by converting a V to X or X to V.
matchstick.example: Turning an X into a V by moving one diagonal elsewhere, leaving the remaining diagonal unchanged, which would produce an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from I to V/X to create VI or XI
matchstick.principle: If the equation can be balanced by adding an I after a V or X, move a vertical stick from an existing I to the V or X, forming VI or XI.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single‑stick vertical transfer can increase a numeral’s value by 1 without breaking other symbols.
matchstick.example: Taking the only stick from an I and leaving a half‑I behind, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Preserve exactly one equals sign
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one ‘=’ operator; you cannot remove or add additional equals signs.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from or added to the ‘=’ sign.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘=’ into ‘-’ and ending up with no equals sign in the equation.

matchstick.title: Target numeral based on arithmetic difference
matchstick.principle: Before moving a stick, compute the Arabic values of both sides, determine the required change, and then select a numeral that can be altered by a single stick move to adjust its value by exactly that difference, ensuring the resulting equation balances.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the given equation is false and you need to decide which character to modify to achieve equality.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick arbitrarily (e.g., turning ‘=’ into ‘-’) without considering the numeric impact, leading to an incorrect equality.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual manipulation of sticks and neglects to compute the Arabic values after the move.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert both sides of the transformed equation to Arabic numbers and check that they are equal before finalising the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets the exact required phrasing or whitespace handling for the final line.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: End the response with a line exactly matching ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’, using uppercase letters and collapsing any extra whitespace.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the operation as removal rather than relocation, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick, explicitly specify a new location for it so that the total stick count remains unchanged.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick from a numeral without ensuring the remaining sticks still form a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move, verify that each numeral still matches a legal Roman‑numeral shape (e.g., X and V must retain two diagonals).

matchstick.description: Creating invalid Roman numeral (e.g., IIII, invalid ordering)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model counts sticks but ignores the syntactic rules of Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that every resulting numeral follows standard Roman‑numeral conventions (no four consecutive I’s, correct subtractive notation, proper ordering).
